examples.name: search_docs
examples.description: Full-text search the project documentation corpus and return up to N matching passages with source URLs. Use this when the user asks about API behavior, configuration, or any factual question about the documented product. Idempotent. Does not modify state.
examples.rationale: Verb-led name, single responsibility, explicit idempotency, bounded result count, clear when-to-use guidance in the description.

examples.name: do_search
examples.rationale: Vague name, useless description, no when-to-use, no bound on result size, cryptic param name (q vs query), no idempotency statement.

examples.name: transfer_funds
examples.description: Move money between two accounts. NON-IDEMPOTENT and IRREVERSIBLE — the caller MUST first confirm with the user. Requires an explicit idempotency_key from the caller; calls with a repeated key return the original result without re-charging.
examples.rationale: Loud about irreversibility, requires idempotency_key, currency pattern constrained, integer cents avoids float rounding.

examples.name: send_money
examples.description: Sends money. Use this to send money.
examples.rationale: Float amount risks rounding, no source account, no currency, no idempotency, no warning about irreversibility. Model will call this confidently and wrongly.

examples.name: lookup_user
examples.description: Look up a user by id.
examples.rationale: Overlaps with get_user below. Two near-identical tools → model picks randomly. Pick one, delete the other.

examples.name: get_user
examples.rationale: Functionally identical to lookup_user — and disagrees on param name. Classic 'tool registry sprawl' pitfall.

pitfalls.title: Vague descriptions
pitfalls.body: If you can't explain in one sentence WHEN to use this tool over the others, the model can't either. Lead with the verb, end with the constraint (idempotent / requires confirmation / read-only / etc).

pitfalls.title: Overlapping tools
pitfalls.body: Two tools with similar descriptions force the model to guess. Worse than one slightly-suboptimal tool. Consolidate or differentiate sharply.

pitfalls.title: Oversized registries
pitfalls.body: Past ~30 tools, models start to forget. Group by domain and route through a 'pick a domain first' supervisor instead of dumping all 80 tools into context.

pitfalls.title: Loose schemas
pitfalls.body: Free-text params get free-text values. Enums, patterns, integer-vs-number, minLength on ids — every constraint is a class of bug the harness catches, not the model.

pitfalls.title: Silent side effects
pitfalls.body: If the tool writes, mark it in the description: 'WRITE', 'IRREVERSIBLE', 'SENDS EMAIL'. The model is dramatically more careful when told. Don't hide it under a friendly name like 'finalize'.

pitfalls.title: No structured errors
pitfalls.body: Tool returns 'oops' as a plain string. Model treats it as data, builds the next step on top of the apology. Always return { ok: false, error: '…' } or set is_error:true.

pitfalls.title: Unbounded result size
pitfalls.body: Tool returns 200 KB. Half gets truncated. Model answers from the first half, confident and wrong. Cap at the tool layer; offer a follow-up tool for pagination.
